source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:23 ('written גיים, read גוים — and every nations-word in the Torah is plene vav with one yod EXCEPT THIS, written with two yods and no vav; so our rabbis expounded: it is written GEYIM' — Avodah Zarah 11a, Bereshit Rabbah, Shochar Tov 9)
claim_en: THE TWO PROUD ONES IN THE WOMB: שני גיים ('TWO NATIONS are in your womb') — the Torah's ONE nations-word written with two yods and no vav (the qere reads גוים): SNAPSHOT carries the written and the read side by side (two-token encoding), and the census locks the rule — bare plene גוים stands 18 times, the lean two-yod form ONCE, here. The Talmud's derash rides the ktiv: read it GEYIM, the two lordly ones — Rebbi and Antoninus at one table (Avodah Zarah 11a).

claim_en: THE TWO-WAY SERVE-VERB: ורב יעבד צעיר ('and the elder shall serve the younger' — or the reverse) — written DEFECTIVE, no vav, and Bereshit Rabbah 63 makes the ambiguity explicit: the lean verb can be read active or passive, 'if worthy... if not' — the oracle's double edge lives in the missing letter. source: Bereshit Rabbah 63:5
claim_en: THE ENTREATY VERB IS DISPUTED, AND THE ANATOMY WITH IT. R. Yochanan reads the verb as pouring out prayer abundantly; Reish Lakish reads it as OVERTURNING the decree, as a pitchfork turns grain on the threshing floor. Beside it the facing-prayer scene - each praying in a different corner, each asking that the children come from the other - and the carved-uterus claim: she had no womb and it was carved for her, the anatomical twin of the same claim made for Sarah at gen_42's credit. The block's opening event is thereby given a mechanism as well as a cause.

source: Onkelos Genesis 25:23
claim_en: THE TRANSLATION SETTLES THE MOST AMBIGUOUS CLAUSE IN THE ORACLE. 'The elder shall serve the younger' does not say in the received ink which noun is subject and which object - the clause is famously reversible. Onkelos renders it decisively: the GREATER shall be SUBJUGATED to the smaller. And 'two peoples' becomes two KINGDOMS. Where the Hebrew leaves the outcome open, the translation closes it and politicizes it in the same breath.

check.note: A structurally ambiguous clause resolved in one direction by the translation, with the terms politicized.

The verse's oracle-consultation becomes a study errand on both legs of the declared reading at once.

claim_en: A LIFESPAN IS READ AS SHORTENED BY EXACTLY THE GAP BETWEEN TWO CENSUS VERSES. The chain reads five years as withheld on account of the crimes charged to the stew day, and the arithmetic is available in our own corpus: Abraham's years are given as 175 at 25:7 and Isaac's as 180 at 35:28 - a difference of exactly five. The claim is that the elder did not live to see what the day contained. Both numbers verified at derivation; the second sits in gen_58, not yet derived.
